findings.title: Stable polygon inset still loses representable miters in painted coverage
findings.related_owner: MarkSpec::leaf lines 781-793 passes the resulting path/miter to kurbo::stroke; kurbo 0.13.1 src/stroke.rs lines 457-468 still uses hypot + dot to decide whether to keep a miter.
findings.body: The new normalized offset succeeds and returns a finite head, but setting head.miter does not make the downstream stroke miter test numerically stable. For nearly opposite edges, hypot + dot rounds to zero and Kurbo drops a mathematically permitted miter. Public MarkDrawable.outline/outline-bounds and placement footprints silently describe a bevelled/truncated polygon instead of the promised grown polygon. The new public checks only require right <= tip + tolerance, so a missing tip or missing wings passes.

reproducers.result: prepare/geometry return success; finite outline stops 100 million drawing units short of its nominal tip
the outer wing extent is about 1/101 of the uniformly grown polygon; right-only assertions still pass

findings.proof: 100-digit independent lobe-inradius calculation establishes the required uniform growth. Independent offset-line intersections of the exact emitted f64 path establish finite convex miter points and verify every such miter is below the emitted limit. Nearby 10x1e-5 triangle and 99.9999% stealth controls pass. Both failures reproduce in hash-qualified current native and exact selected public WASM.
findings.requested_change: Carry the stable miter construction through actual painted-outline/footprint generation for these representable accepted polygons. Add complete bounds or corner-coverage regressions for thin triangles and deep stealth wings, rather than only upper-bounding the front. Preserve accepted geometry; do not classify these finite cases as true degeneracy or silently substitute bevels.

round1_findings.detail: Identical old review executable freshly gives 3 failures / 1 passing control; corrected executable passes all four unchanged assertions. The two old numerical examples also pass public WASM. The normalized offset eliminates the fallback and fixed-resolution bisection, but the same accepted positive-polygon contract fails downstream as A2-P2-1.

round1_findings.finding: P2 signed full-turn barb rear contact
round1_findings.detail: Actual signed interval [-sweep/2,+sweep/2] always contains crossing 0; bounded |sweep|<=TAU makes integer enumeration safe and finite. Exact signed turns include +/-PI and rear contact 9.5, adjacent open turns retain front contact .5; reversal maps both contacts and gives 4.5. Fresh native/public tests cover signed full/nearest-float-open/zero/partial/reversal/curve/composite cases. Native next-after-outside-domain controls reject as before.
Imported at test module scope; both patterns use the imported type. No unrelated Rust policy departures found in the correction.

geometry_audit.normalized_construction: Parameter-derived positive_area is independent of underflowed products. Normalized dart notch retains inset-1, binary vector scaling avoids avoidable vector-normalization rounding, compensated determinant and half-angle forms replace the previous 1+cos cutoff. Linear edge contraction removes the 64-step absolute bisection. No growth iteration/nontermination, no uninset success fallback for positive stroked polygons.
geometry_audit.degeneracy_and_limits: Fresh minimum-positive uniform triangle/square/diamond with unit stroke remain accepted and finite; zero dimensions/100% notch retain their explicit as-given exception, zero stroke preserves tiny coordinates. A 1 x minimum-positive triangle reports explicit unrepresentable offset error. This does not qualify all f64 dynamic ranges or all rasterizers. Four public +/-minimum-subnormal-radian barb cases fail explicitly at placement with nonfinite geometry on BOTH old and corrected WASM; they are a pre-existing limit, not credited as passing contacts.
geometry_audit.curve_tolerance: New public curved control keeps the geometric 9.5 chord at 1e-8 and shaft/back comparison at 1e-6. PreparedCarrier::new calls unchanged PathTrimmer::new(...,1e-6). curve_api.rs unchanged. All pre-existing native and public assertions are unchanged; the new tolerance is justified by the existing owner.
geometry_audit.public_and_source_scope: R2 production Rust changes are confined to marks.rs; public names/options/validation/wire/stubs stay unchanged. Three unit tests and appended public boundary controls are added; PathSeg usages are corrected. No unrelated physics/numerator/callback expansion. Current source file hash 436a62c231b0bbf49fae9101eb0f89edd2bbad888df0c593fa126d1f9f5c3f49.
geometry_audit.visual_inspection: Fresh ordinary and boundary gallery SVG/PNG renders byte-match the candidate in both themes and were viewed. Ordinary marks, full/signed/reversed barbs, composites and curve contacts appear consistent. Full extents of extreme thin/deep cases are subpixel; near-flat cropped tip is visible, thin cropped tip remains visually empty at that display scale. These views do not certify extreme coverage; strict numerical controls found A2-P2-1.
